conventions.convention: General mutual information is directional joint-law KL in nats, assumes AC, and does not require Lebesgue densities.
The general information rate-distortion function is an infimum over couplings with the fixed source marginal, measured in bits by dividing KL by ln 2; an empty feasible infimum is infinity.
Block distortion is the normalized additive sum for positive blocklength; coordinate labels may start at zero or one without changing the normalization.
Operational codes are deterministic and fixed-length. The excess criterion requires convergence at D + ε for every ε > 0, not at the exact threshold D.
Finite-alphabet information rate-distortion uses nonempty finite alphabets, finite nonnegative distortion, and bit mutual information; infeasible budgets below D_min have value infinity.
Stationary block quantities use two-sided stationary finite-alphabet sources and bits per symbol. R_erg ranges over jointly stationary ergodic pairs with the specified source marginal.
Gaussian vector distortion is total squared Euclidean error per vector, not error divided by dimension. Zero-variance coordinates contribute zero, including log-positive at zero.

Blahut–Arimoto starts at t = 0 with positive source probabilities and full-support q_0. Its objective and gap tolerance are in nats. Certified interval execution additionally requires rational inputs and positive rational tolerance; no bit-complexity bound is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: For a stationary finite-alphabet source and bounded additive distortion, R_n(D) converges to inf_n R_n(D) = R_block(D) at every feasible D. R_block is nonincreasing and convex on [D_min, infinity), zero for D ≥ D_c, right-continuous at D_min, and infinite below D_min.

Assume AC. For a stationary ergodic finite-alphabet source with bounded distortion, any feasible D ≥ D_min and any r > R_block(D) admit a jointly stationary ergodic source/reconstruction pair with the given source marginal, mean distortion at most D, and limsup bit mutual-information rate strictly below r.

For nonempty finite alphabets, a source pmf and finite nonnegative distortion, the feasible channel set is nonempty exactly when D ≥ D_min. Whenever nonempty, mutual information in bits attains its minimum.
Assume AC. If X has law N(0, σ²), σ² > 0, Y is any jointly distributed real reconstruction, and 0 < D < σ² with E(X − Y)² ≤ D, then I_nat(X;Y) ≥ (1/2) ln(σ²/D), without a density assumption on Y.

For finite nonempty source and reproduction alphabets and finite nonnegative distortion, R(D) is finite, nonincreasing and convex on [D_min, infinity), zero for D ≥ D_c, and right-continuous at every feasible distortion, including D_min.

For m ≥ 1 nonnegative variances λ_i and 0 < D < sum_i λ_i, the unique positive water level solves sum_i min(λ_i, θ) = D; the allocation δ_i = min(λ_i, θ) minimizes the stated coordinate-rate sum. The lemma separately specifies D = 0, zero variances and D ≥ sum_i λ_i.

For an iid finite-alphabet source, finite nonempty reproduction alphabet and finite nonnegative distortion, both expected-distortion and positive-slack excess-distortion operational rates equal the finite information rate-distortion function for every D ≥ 0, with value infinity below D_min.

concerns.concern: The displayed reconstruction needs X_2 independent of (U,V), which is not explicitly specified. The Statement gives X_1 independent of X_2 and says only that U,V are independent standard normals; step 2.1 then invokes the vector theorem to conclude attainment. Those independence assertions alone do not suffice: take independent standard normals Z_1,Z_2, set X_1=2Z_1, X_2=Z_2, a=√(5/2), b=√(3/2), U=(aZ_1+bZ_2)/2 and V=(bZ_1−aZ_2)/2. Then U,V are independent standard normals and X_1=aU+bV, as written, but Y_1=aU is a nonconstant deterministic continuous function of the full source vector, giving infinite vector mutual information. The intended independent-coordinate test-channel construction is immediate from F2; explicitly choosing X_2 independently of (U,V) closes the gap.

The assigned seam says this page requires rate-distortion-and-lossy-source-coding, and its item thm-it-point-to-point-lossy-source-channel-separation explicitly imports that page's information RDF, attainment, operational coding theorem and right-continuity results in F1, F2 and F5. seams_checked.note: The source definition uses the same two-sided left shift. The block arguments preserve bit entropy, and the stationary coding theorem uses the ergodic SMB limit and stationary entropy-rate limit under their finite-alphabet hypotheses.

The information bound and lossy separation theorem preserve finite iid hypotheses, feasible distortion, deterministic fixed-length codes, positive-slack excess criteria and bit-to-nat conversion. The missing page requires declaration is reported separately in alerts.

The Wyner–Ziv and multiterminal code definitions use the same normalized finite additive distortion. They explicitly use nats for their own rates and do not import the memoryless RDF theorem as a side-information coding theorem.

The finite squared-error quantizer definition faithfully identifies its integral as expected single-letter squared-error distortion. The page's empirical optimization and restricted compact high-rate results make no unsupported operational RDF identification.
